review_candidates.description: Kamoto Copper Company Société Anonyme, KCC SA in acronym, is a Congolese company operating in Kolwezi, capital of the province of Lualaba, in the Democratic Republic of Congo. KCC SA exploits copper and cobalt ores on a large scale. It includes an underground mine, open-pit mines and integrated metallurgical facilities. The operation has one of the largest copper reserves in the world, with a current life of over 25 years. As an industrial mining company, we provide safe workplaces and support the sustainable development of the local economy. We maintain a constructive and open dialogue with the communities that host us, as well as with the provincial and national government. Job Description. Reporting directly to the Manager – TSF Construction, the incumbent will be responsible for planning, coordinating, supervising, and ensuring the successful completion of infrastructure projects associated with tailings storage facilities (TSF). He/She will ensure that projects are executed in compliance with health, safety, environmental, and quality requirements, engineering plans, and approved timelines and budgets. The position will also involve coordinating multidisciplinary teams, contractors, and consultants involved in the projects. In this capacity, he/she will contribute to the development and commissioning of reliable TSF infrastructure that meets technical standards and the company's operational needs. His/Her responsibilities will include, but are not limited to: Planning and managing the execution of TSF infrastructure projects includes preparing execution plans, construction schedules, work packages, resource requirements, and monitoring projects from launch to completion and handover to operational teams. Supervising the construction and development of TSF infrastructure includes supervision of access and transport roads, embankments, drainage and water management systems, tailings and water pipelines, settling structures, spillway and diversion works, as well as other civil, mechanical and electrical infrastructure required for TSF operations. Coordinating engineering and construction activities includes collaborating with engineering teams and consultants, reviewing plans, technical specifications, execution methods and construction plans, and verifying constructability and compliance of works with approved designs. Managing contractors and subcontractors includes monitoring their performance in terms of safety, quality, costs and deadlines, verifying the availability of necessary resources, equipment and skills, and coordinating daily and weekly construction activities. Monitoring costs, deadlines and project progress includes tracking expenditures against approved budgets, early identification of risks of cost or schedule overruns, analysis of contractor claims and variations, and implementation of appropriate corrective actions. Managing project risks and HSE requirements includes promoting visible leadership in health, safety and environment, verifying the application of risk assessments, permits and safe work procedures, and stopping or escalating work when an unacceptable risk is identified. Ensuring quality control of construction work includes coordinating with QA/QC teams, monitoring inspections and tests, reviewing non-conformities and corrective actions, and verifying that the work complies with specifications, technical standards and project requirements. Coordinating interfaces between different stakeholders includes collaborating with engineering, construction, operations, maintenance, procurement, consultants, contractors and other departments to resolve technical and operational constraints and ensure efficient project execution. project governance and reporting includes preparing regular reports on progress, costs, deadlines, risks, quality and performance, maintaining reliable documentation and presenting updates to management and relevant stakeholders. Coordinating the commissioning and transfer of infrastructure includes verifying the completion of work and defects, the availability of certificates, test results, "as- built " plans and other required documents, as well as coordinating the formal transfer of infrastructure to the Operations and/or Maintenance teams and capitalizing on lessons learned. Have a good knowledge of civil engineering works, earthworks, embankment construction and hydraulic infrastructure.
